item.title: Deletions 70: If the fact will not fit the theory – let the theory go.
item.content:encoded:
All Staff-enacted Deletions are carried out according to the Deletions Guide.

Summary deletions result for:

  • Articles with malicious intent
  • Pages that are clearly unfinished.
  • Attempts to "game" site procedure, such as re-posting a non-rewritten article in an attempt to get around downvotes.
  • Blatantly plagiarized material.
  • An article posted outside of the current range.

If an author attempts to self-delete their work and fails to do so properly, including either by blanking the page or renaming it, it will be deleted properly by Staff.

item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Readers & Reviewers
item.content:encoded:
Note: If you're going to introduce yourself here, please scroll down and click "New Post" and NOT "reply", otherwise your comment will nest incorrectly!

Hello, readers and reviewers of the Foundation Universe!

This month's random question is: what kind of random thoughts keep you up at night?

Let's start off with some things to take a look at to enhance your reading, now that you're a site member:

  • If you have any questions about the Foundation'verse and its various individuals and groups of interest, head over to the Foundation Universe forum to talk about the various aspects of living/working/being in constant fear of a world where anomalies are real.
  • Did you know our site has a night mode version? If you're interested in that (and a few other neat things!), check out our Usertools page.
  • Want to leave a comment or read others' thoughts on something you've read recently? Scroll down to the bottom of that page you read, click the "Discuss" link, and take a look at the comments others have posted!

For those looking to put your knowledge of the SCP-verse to work and contribute to the site by helping develop works-in-progress, head on over to the Writing Help forums!

  • So you want to be a concept reviewer?
  • So you want to be a draft reviewer?
  • And of course, remember the Criticism Policy!

If you're not sure what to talk about here, you can take a look at our How to Write an Intro/Welcome thread for ideas.

Go ahead and respond to other new members if you find that your interests overlap, and definitely ask for reading suggestions if there's a particular kind of SCP article or tale you enjoy reading. If you're looking to get started as a critiquer, feel free to mention the kind of material you particularly want to see more of on the wiki! You might even see some of our authors drop by here from time to time, if you mention you liked their work! :)

Welcome to the site!

Hello, prospective site writers! It's good to see you here!

This month's random question is: what kind of random thoughts keep you up at night?

First off, a couple standard things to keep in mind as you get started towards adding your voice to the Foundation universe:

  • Definitely read the How to Write an SCP Guide and the pages in the Guide Hub that are relevant to your ideas!
  • Make a sandbox page for your works in progress, reference notes, inspirational snippets, and more author things!
  • Get familiar with our three Writing Help Forums:
    • Questions Desk: For all your questions about the writing process!
    • Ideas and Brainstorming: For asking about concepts that you're thinking of writing up! This is an especially important step for first-time authors!
    • Drafts and Critiques: For reviews of your finished pieces, to see what edits need to be made to your work to make it ready for the mainlist!

If you're not sure what to talk about here, you can take a look at our How to Write an Intro/Welcome thread for ideas.

Feel free to respond to other new members if you find that your writing interests and/or plans overlap. The SCP wiki is a collaborative writing community, after all! You might even see some of the longtime writers here drop by with comments now and then. :)

Welcome to the site!

item.title: The Candy Cane
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror and History

Page Layout (Optional): N/A

Elevator Pitch: The SCP I envisioned is a plastic candy cane filled with small M&M-like candies that have different outcomes to it. While one candy that was eaten will give a person something like a lost possession or make them feel happy another could have immense tragedy or have the person who ate it either die or vanish through a trans dimensional entry way or property while a small select few saying that they are speaking for the candy cane.

Central Narrative: The story is mainly about how the candies affected history and while they test the object it shows some form of sentience and claims to have caused some of the worst tragedies and triumphs in history and saying that they had been the first thing consumed and will be the last thing consumed by man.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This is just an idea that I had and wanted to share. While some SCP’s are intriguing for their gruesome nature and such I think an SCP that is more based on luck and a way to solve some of the worlds greater mysteries and why certain things happened would be a intriguing idea.

Additional Notes: I just have a problem of answering a genre. However, I am pretty confident in this even with a hiccup in that department. I will except all the feedback I can get because this one I want to see through till the end and make this my first SCP entry.

item.title: Re: SCP Early concept: the greatest artist
item.content:encoded:
I really like the idea here, I think it's pretty unique, but I'm a little confused with how the immortality and multiple identities work. You say the scp is impossible to kill, but can die. Does this mean that it is impervious to any weapons, but can die from old age or disease? and in that case, does it just live a normal human life span until dying and being reincarnated as one of the 10 different forms? If that is how it works, I think a cool idea to add would be that within each of its life spans, it, as you describe, goes from asking for basic supplies, to more extreme mediums, and at the end of each life span it attempts to do something SUPER dangerous and the foundation has to do something to stop it each time. I'm not sure how dangerous art could be lol, but maybe you could think of something.

item.title: Re: Seeking Greenlight: Fireproof SAR Dog
item.content:encoded:
Right now, I’m not getting what I should really be paying attention to in this story. Is it the anomalous abilities themselves? Is it the fire department this dog was working for? You mention in the beginning that this dog can control small fires, but you never bring that up again. I don’t know if talking about SAR missions where a dog happened to be safe would really be interesting. here’s a guide that I think explains the problem I’m seeing. I’ll paraphrase a bit. Right now you have a very simple anomaly, which is fine, but you’re going to want to add a bit more depth if you really want to grab the reader’s attention. That being said, you do actually have certain directions you can go with this. If you want to focus on the SAR part of this then you might want to expand on the dog’s powers some more. If you want to focus on the dog itself then you might want to show the extent of its abilities, maybe throw some logical extremes in there. There’re of course other paths you can take with this, those are just two ways to go.


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: Seeking Greenlight: Fireproof SAR Dog

item.title: Author Post!
item.content:encoded:
Big big big thanks to my lovely reviewers in chat: Pratten, Savan, Calibri_Bold, Mars, chaucer345, and Karakatt for all your wonderful suggestions to better develop the backstory here!

Image source is here: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Common_earwig_(Forficula_auricularia)_on_thumb.jpg

Notes:
- All of Wiggy’s interview excerpt dialogue consists of words found in the Wikipedia article for Earwig: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earwig
- Why earwigs? 1. When I was in elementary school, my friends and I found a very large pincher bug on the playground and admired it. Some other kid picked it up and tore off its pincers to keep as a souvenir. That image has stuck with me for over a decade. I can’t smush earwigs anymore. Also last month I found one in a box at work the other day and I let him go outside and it reminded me of that incident. 2. Quoth Wikipedia, “Earwigs are among the few non-social insect species that show maternal care.” Pinchy pinch moms are good moms. There’s a lot of neat facts about earwigs.
- Why Arizona? During my background research, I found this: https://cals.arizona.edu/yavapai/anr/hort/byg/archive/earwig.html so I just went with Arizona.

Best wishes to everyone in this crazy year. To everyone who has the opportunity to nurture a life, no matter how small, and those who teach others to do the same, you are the hope of the world.

item.title: The Bartender
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror/Drama

Elevator Pitch: A humanoid SCP that is approximately from 6 to 15 feet tall, dressed up in a bartender suit of the mid-1900s, and has its general appearance as a tall black figure that has devoid facial features, and no sign of hair, nose, eyes, has unchecked limitations, and numerous of anomalous abilities. In all of which, it is in foundation custody. The Foundation's goal was to prevent its anomalous abilities from attempting to cause out an event of containment breaches by accident. The containment procedure was to keep SCP-XXXX inside a 16 x 60 ft (about 3.7 x 5.5m) room constructed out of tungsten.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX is a humanoid entity dressed up in a bartender suit of the mid-1900s, comprised of a white shirt, a black or red tie, black trousers, and black shoes. It measures 6 to 15 feet tall has a general appearance as a tall black figure. However, it is possible that this is not SCP-XXXX's true form and that it is an eldritch being that cannot comprehend whose proper form. Its face is pitch black, utterly devoid of facial features. Despite lacking facial features, SCP-XXXX can sense when its targets are near at all times, as it never hesitates and always sees the targets around it. SCP-XXXX has various anomalous abilities that the Foundation was to yet discovered. The ones learned so far are based on the logs of the incident, description, experiments, and interviewing logs of the Foundation, which are:

+ show block
– hide block
  • Teleportation.
  • Mind-affecting.
  • Memory adding, erasing, and inhibiting.
  • Causing instant death by making eye contact with a subject longer than three (3) seconds.
  • Extremely high superhuman attributes.
  • Causing out technological disruption upon technologies in random moments without wanting it to do so.
  • Able to sense how dangerous the ones it confronts are.
  • The ability to let it cause out phenomenons to become an omnipresent being that can warp space and time between locations, or possibly reality.
  • Strong regenerative healing factor.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The idea of having an SCP with an unknown past and couldn't remember a lot of who it was before becoming a humanoid entity that has various extremely dangerous and powerful anomalous abilities.

Additional Notes: I couldn't figure it out. People said that my grammar was having problems, but I've fixed my grammar errors and even improved my SCP article. What am I really missing?


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: voodoo doll that when picked up, causes the subject to fly into rage against the last person to anger them, the voodoo doll will take on the appearance of that person, and the subject will use it to kill the victim by any means available. These people are now known as SCP-XXX-1(Subject) and -2(victim). When the victim is killed, the doll reverts to its original form and repairs all damage, the subject will then lose their memory of interacting with the doll. After event XXX-01, it is discovered that the doll has a cognitohazard effect that makes people want to use it.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: In an addendum, event XXX-01 is described, along with an interrogation log and security tape transcript, where a guard unknowingly uses the scp to kill his boss while patrolling the anomalous item vault the object was contained in. It is investigated and found that the SCP has developed a new property while in containment, the O5 council releases a statement acknowledging the threat posed by this and suggests the development of an Emergent Properties Research Division (EPRD), in order to study the possible ‘evolution’ of anomalous properties in contained SCPs. The SCP is reclassified from safe to euclid, and containment protocols are updated

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The main hook here is the emergent properties idea. I don’t think I’ve ever read an article that mentions SCPs ‘evolving’ new anomalous properties, and I explain it in the article as an adaptation made by the SCP in order to affect people while still in containment. I think it’s just a cool new thing to add to the lore, as well as creating a new branch of the foundation in the EPRD

Additional Notes: As mentioned in the title, I am a first time writer, so all criticism is welcome. I’ve been reading SCPs for years so I think I have a grasp on how to write them, but we’ll see how this is received. I have the full article written in my sandbox if you’d like to just read it.

item.title: The Stalker (Looking for Green Light)
item.content:encoded:
A SCP that is always around a present, first you just saw it once at work, now no matter where you are it is always there.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror, Emotional

Elevator Pitch: The idea is a SCP that slowly creeps into the victim's life. At first he’s a random face in the street, not unlike the hundreds of unknown faces you pass everyday. But over time he's just there more often, now he's at the commissary, at your favorite restaurant, and you swear you saw him through your front window. Wait was he that person you just saw out the corner of your eye? This process then repeats but quicker with hearing him everywhere and then even quicker with feeling his presence everywhere. After this it seems he's not only around you at all times, but now he's in your head. Every moment, every thought he's there.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: The SCP article will be told through a series of interviews and documents. The central story is a chronological story told by a series of interviews and other documents. It starts with a victim recounting his story as defined in the hook below, and then followed by his missing papers. This man is the first known victim of the SCP and causes the SCP foundation to launch an operation into the man's town to try and find the SCP (told through a OPORD). While they do find the SCP it escapes by unknown means but one of the SCP agents gets infected by the SCP and is put into quarantine. After a month in quarantine being a SCP scientist checking on the Agent is infected and the Agent seemingly disappeared. The infected scientist escapes to the original victim's town, the rest of the story is finding why the SCP is attracted to here.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The hook will be an interview between a SCP Scientist and a SCP victim. In the interview the victim, clearly traumatized by what's happening to him, recounts his story of how the SCP is everywhere. It's basically the elevator pitch in more detail. I put a *rough* draft for this interview below if yall want to see how this will look in execution.

Additional Notes: I'm not sure if this is similar to any other SCP, please tell me if it is. Note the final step after the SCP is always present in the victim's mind is eventually the victim becomes the SCP, still the same person, but now that person is the SCP.

Hook Rough Draft

Rough draft, I know this doesn't follow SCP Interview Protocols, will fix it in actual.
“I don't know who he is, no, I can’t even tell what he is. Everytime I go out he’s there, he’s a waiter, a random face in a crowd, or even my own co-worker, but no matter what he’s always there. It just doesn't make sense, he can’t physically be everywhere, no it's definitely impossible, it's unnatural. How can a single man be everywhere? Even when I'm in the safety of my own home… What cruel joke do I mean by saying safety, I hear his goddamn voice there too! Whether i’m eating or sleeping, his voice is just there. At first it was just another random voice I heard at work, you know one of those hundreds of random background voices you hear every day, but then I started hearing it more and more. Now *sob*, now it's all I can hear, for the love of god I don’t want to hear that wretched thing anymore. Even now, I see it, I hear it, … my god, it's here, I can feel it. *addressing SCP Scientist* Why, why is it here, you told me I would be safe here, but it's here. I know it's here, I can feel it! *standing up*Come out demon, where are you hiding!! *falling to the floor* Please, please just leave me alone.”

This should have a question mark or maybe ?!

"I read your file… They will get you eventually… The GOC doesn't leave loose ends." He says as you hold the gun to his head. You pull the trigger.

Akhiabara, Japan

Pretty sure Akhiabara is just a district of Tokyo

Echo: We are on the 3rd floor…

Suggest adding in contractions, people don’t usually say “We are” they say “We’re”… this goes for any spoken dialogue

The reality instability is shown to be at its most extreme, and has caused the hallway leading out of the stairwell to stretch infinitely.

So you explain a little but I would describe more here… “most extreme” seems worse than the Hallway extending forever.//

The living room is in complete fluctuation, and in the middle is a young girl around the age of 14.

Suggest explaining the fluctuations.. then break out the description of the girl in another sentence, also suggest saying “young teenager girl” as its hard to guess age by looking.

  • I think the end sorta fizzles… why did he decide to take the target? Why does he feel this way? Those are questions could be left unanswered… but the time between Roach turning on his teammate and then the events played out earlier. Think you need to explain that too somewhere

item.content:encoded:
It's a cool concept, but it's a bit too corny for me. I'm not sure if switching Discord for a fictional app would have made it any better, but here are some parts that bothered me the most:

as Discord is known for its humorous loading screens.

To me this is too informal for an scp article. The article doesn't have to justify why a reader of the terms of service would think of it as a joke since anyone reading the article could understand why.

I started one of the bloodiest wars in history because I wasn't invited to a wedding.

I don't know a lot about Greek/Roman mythology so to me this is either: 1. A random assertion unrelated to any known myth, and so kind of pointless or 2. A reference to a myth, meaning that 5721-1 hasn't done anything better for the last 2000 years.

But then I remembered a tiny, tiny detail. I've read The Daily Crier. In fact, I read it pretty much every day. And I've never even seen the name Chelsea Reynolds pop up even once.

It seems kind of silly to me that the Foundation would send an operative with a half-assed disguise that can be proven false with publically available information. Given that they have to spread misinformation on a somewhat regular basis and even have an MTF dedicated to that it wouldn't be so surprising to find a few agents that have been working in a news organization.

Overall it's a cool concept, especially the idea that people nowadays wouldn't take a deal with the devil seriously even if they had already signed it. But it has quite a few things that bother me.

So I'm no voting

item.title: Re: Greenlight request- Frozen Corpse and Nervous System
item.content:encoded:
+ show block
– hide block

What are the origins of this anomaly?

The implications I'm making are that the fetus developed a mutation that absorbed the mother's brain matter into itself, then caused the rest of its body to dissolve and sink into the legs. The nervous system in the legs pulls itself away from the top half.

What closure would you think would make sense?

The skip manages to use all its effort in the observation session to make it clear it wants to return to a family member (causing the top half to whisper), but can't manage to do it a second time, and its attempts are thus dismissed as too speculative for the researchers to take action on. So much time is spent on trying to recreate the circumstances to repeat the message it left in the recorded session that it ends up consuming too much of its own body and deflates, becoming sluggish and close to death. The lead scientist decides to freeze it indefinitely until a solid answer on whether the mutation can happen again is found, or if a way to regenerate the consumed tissue is discovered. Essentially it's a downer ending as the skip can't get what it wants, despite its hardships. Because its still technically alive at the end, it's left open-ended, though. Do you think it should not be open-ended?

And then how could you imply those things without maybe explicitly stating them?

The origin is implied in the description section. I mention the shrunken portions of the brain that control cognition, motor functions, memory, etc, without explicitly stating their function- it just says frontal lobe, parietal lobe, and hippocampus without explaining to the reader why that's significant; I don't intend to talk down to them. I mention that the bisecting tear is along the uterus and the pattern of the tear suggests that the woman was pulled apart rather than cut in half, but that there are no markings or scars to suggest that an outside force caused it, leading the reader to consider that something inside her caused the bisection (the fetus, which is listed as cryptically missing or nonexistent). I mention the DNA in the living neurons are a near match to the corpse, implying that it is not a foreign force taking over the legs, but either living remains of the fetus and/or the woman herself.

The conclusion is implied in the addenda. The first addendum is the audio file where the top half's whisper is heard, and the transcript where the whisper is excluded. This is called to the listener's attention beforehand when the scientist stops, claiming he thinks he saw an arm move, implying that there is life in the top half.

The second addendum mentions that other researchers heard the whisper, describing it as an indiscriminate noise, and recommended further research in case it meant something (without mentioning what the whisper said, or that it was even a whisper). The lead scientist recreates the situation several times in hopes that it will happen again and tests for living tissue in the throat and mouth but repeatedly finds nothing and eventually dismisses the whole argument that it made any significant sound. This hints to the reader that it may have spoken something, so they will listen to the audio file closely and try to decipher it on their own.

The third addendum simply mentions that it has consumed itself too much during its time outside the freezer and will be preserved cryogenically, rather than through conventional freezing.

Basically, I'm hoping to get the readers to piece the puzzle together on their own through both reading and listening, which I think would make a unique experience, but that's up to you if you agree.

so just a gory description of this anomaly isn’t really story rich, or all that unique

This is part of the reason I intend to add the audio file, not just for the story, but for the sound effects the skip makes, (cracking, sloshing, banging, skittering, etc.) and the scientist's reactions, which I think will add to the discomfort factor (I know audio is what made SCP-682 so infamous, not that my intention is to mimic that article). Without the audio I understand how the description might seem tame, but again, it's up to you if you think this is worth trying.

item.title: Re: *Seeking Green-light**(S)pecialized (C)ustodial (P)ersonnel
item.content:encoded:
As a counterpoint to the "Don't make this an MTF" opinions:

There's sort of two good ideas here, both of them interesting in their own way. Both of them would be great examples of something I've long thought we needed more stories about, the tales of the support crew side of the Foundation. Somebody has to mop up after Testing Bay 3 is flooded with ectoplasm and change the lightbulbs in the Keter wing, and they're bound to have some great stories.

The story you have in your elevator pitch is good idea one- every site needs its custodial crew, and I could see the character you describe as the star of a whole series of stories from whodunnit mysteries to small-scale horror about his own bad days. He and his crew don't need to be an MTF, just the people with the keys to the supply closest and enough guts or crazy to not quit the first time hallway 6B starts screaming. (It just does that sometimes.)

Good idea two is an MTF, or rather an underutilized type of MTF. Not all MTFs run into danger guns blazing or defy death crawling through tunnels that may or may not pass through literal hell. The big list-o-MTFs has a bunch of MTFs with support or utility missions- for instance MTF-ϒ-7("Cavity Creeps") is primarily composed of dentists. There is one existing MTF that specializes in hazmat-type situations- MTF-Β-7("Maz Hatters")- and it makes sense that there would be similar counterparts that specialize in things like rebuilding destroyed sites (it does happen with uncomfortable regularity), constructing the various odd containment cells required for certain SCPs1, figure out how to relocate the garden full of talking plants… There's stories to be told there, but not this one.

Footnotes
1. we need a 10 meter radius concrete chamber within .001% of perfectly spherical coated in 30,000 tiles with "Asparagus" written on them by hand in 6 languages. We estimate it will breach temporary containment in a month.
